name: Bones & Ledger
description: A deliberately analog dice-and-betting game played with hand-carved bone or ceramic dice and a paper ledger sheet, requiring zero technology and leaving no digital trace. Players bet on sequential dice rolls against a communal 'ledger' that tracks debts across the table, with the twist that debts can be inherited by other players mid-game, creating cascading obligation chains that mirror Shelf credit systems. The game's design is attributed to a collective of Tier 1 labor organizers who wanted something untraceable and ungoverned.
story_hooks: A set of bone dice carved in 2183 has passed through hundreds of games and is considered a Shelf artifact — someone has stolen them from the bar where they lived, and the community wants them back.

A player discovers that the ledger mechanic, when played with exactly seven players using a specific rule variant, produces debt cascade patterns that map precisely to a real corponation's internal credit structure — someone designed this intentionally.
A Tier 4 anthropologist has been attending Shelf Bones & Ledger games as 'research' and is about to publish a paper that will bring unwanted attention — and surveillance — to the community.
